newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Ireland questioned about threat of inflation.
newsitem.headline: Ireland questioned about threat of inflation.

text.p: European Union countries endorsed Ireland's economic performance on Monday, but questioned whether inflation might not be set to rise, Irish Finance Minister Ruairi Quinn told reporters.
Quinn said his fellow ministers had been complimentary about Ireland's economic convergance programme, one of the most successful in the 15-nation bloc.

But he said that during a discussion at a ministerial meeting Finland and Portugal had asked about the sustainability of Ireland's inflation rate, currently running at about 2.2 percent, up from 1.6 percent last year.
"The fear of inflation is perhaps stronger now because of the punt's value to the pound sterling. We don't know how long that will last," Quinn said he told the ministers.
"If sterling were to stay high in the future, that would bring inflationary pressure on the Irish economy," he added.
